feedback: The confession follows the available chain closely: Chip acknowledges the foil-backed closure material, concealed opening, and later use of the unattended glass. It supplies the exact opening moment and his knowledge of the closure weakness, but those are explanatory details rather than new decisive evidence needed to accuse him. The material denial, admitted glass handling, and falsified insurance date had already made the case. His final reference to trusted hands gives the profession emotional weight and feels earned, though the statement is unusually clear and analytical for someone exposed. Hugh and Barb retain consequences for separate misconduct instead of receiving complete moral absolution, which makes the ending more satisfying. I did not need the finale to discover the killer.
